collection: NERDC JSS 1 Intermediate Science federal bush-fire and charcoal regulation
note: Original classroom practice based on cited Nigerian federal regulations. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Intermediate Science
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish notification of a proposed burn from permission under a Nigerian federal regulation.
questions.prompt: For a civics display, a pupil writes that a farmer's letter telling neighbours about an intended open burn counts as a permit. Under regulations 3 and 4 of Nigeria's federal 2011 bush and forest fire regulations, what is missing and which agency issues the permit?
questions.answer: The letter is missing a permit from the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency, NESREA. Telling neighbours about a proposal does not supply the agency's permission.
questions.explanation: The regulations identify the issuing body and require permission for open burning.

markingGuide.description: Names NESREA or gives its full name.

questions.subject: Intermediate Science
questions.learningObjective: Recognise a purpose expressly prohibited by the federal bush-fire text.
questions.prompt: A fictional account says a group planned to burn bush to drive out animals for hunting. The group argues that the general permit rules make this purpose acceptable. How does regulation 19 of Nigeria's federal 2011 bush and forest fire regulations address the plan?
questions.answer: Regulation 19 expressly prohibits burning bush or forest to hunt animals. The general provisions about permits do not erase that prohibition.
questions.explanation: The purpose of the burning is decisive for applying this provision.

markingGuide.description: Identifies hunting animals as the purpose covered by regulation 19.
States that bush or forest burning for that purpose is prohibited.

questions.subject: Intermediate Science
questions.learningObjective: Explain why the fire notification provision asks for factual details.
questions.prompt: A case study describes a bush fire on occupied land. A draft notification gives the location but leaves out both when the fire happened and any information about its origin. Identify the two missing details listed in regulation 20(1)(a) and (b) of Nigeria's federal 2011 bush and forest fire regulations.
questions.answer: The draft omits the date of the fire and its cause or origin. If the cause is unknown, the writer should say so instead of guessing.
questions.explanation: A dated account and an accurate description of known evidence help a reader understand the incident.

questions.subject: Intermediate Science
questions.learningObjective: Explain a federal measure that addresses habitat loss from charcoal production.
questions.prompt: A fictional commercial charcoal proposal includes plans for production and sales but says nothing about restoring the area where the trees would come from. Under regulation 6(3) of Nigeria's federal 2014 charcoal regulations, which plan is missing and why is it relevant to deforestation?
questions.answer: A reforestation and rehabilitation plan for the source area is missing. It addresses how tree cover and affected land could be restored after removal.
questions.explanation: The cited provision makes planning for restoration a condition of a production permit.

markingGuide.description: Names reforestation and rehabilitation for the source area.
Connects the plan to loss and restoration of tree cover or habitat.

questions.subject: Intermediate Science
questions.subtopic: Choosing where production must be excluded
questions.learningObjective: Explain how a source restriction protects a fragile ecosystem.
questions.prompt: A fictional commercial charcoal producer submits a restoration plan but proposes obtaining the trees from an area identified as a fragile ecosystem. Under regulation 6(4) of Nigeria's federal 2014 charcoal regulations, why does the restoration plan leave a problem?
questions.answer: Regulation 6(4) forbids producing charcoal from fragile ecosystems. The proposal still relies on an excluded source even though it includes a restoration plan.
questions.explanation: The source exclusion and the restoration condition are separate safeguards.

markingGuide.description: Identifies fragile ecosystems as excluded sources.
Explains why the restoration plan does not remove the source restriction.

questions.subject: Intermediate Science
questions.subtopic: Recognising the scope of a rule
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish a specific federal charcoal rule from a universal rule about trees.
questions.prompt: A school poster says the federal 2014 regulations on charcoal prove that every tree-felling decision in Nigeria is governed by those regulations. Use regulations 1 and 2 to explain what is wrong with the poster.
questions.answer: These regulations address charcoal production and handling, including tree felling for charcoal and specified trade and export activities. They also exclude charcoal used for subsistence purposes. Other tree-felling activity needs its own applicable source.
questions.explanation: A claim about all tree felling goes beyond the stated application of this instrument.

markingGuide.description: Explains why the instrument alone cannot establish a rule for all tree felling.
